title: curveFromCSV
body:
## curveFromCSV

Reads point coordinates from named columns of a numeric CSV table and sweeps the same round tube as polylineTube along them (rows in file order, 2 to 1024 rows). With zColumn empty the curve is planar at z = 0. The file is copied into the run directory and its SHA-256 digest is checked, so a measured or simulated trajectory becomes a reproducible presentation mesh.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Every cell of the CSV, including unused columns, must be a finite number under a UTF-8 header row; text columns fail with INVALID_TABLE.
- Coordinates are used as Blender units without conversion; rescale with transform if the table is in millimetres.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `curveFromCSV`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material` | one node | yes | `material` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | Path of the CSV table: a UTF-8 header row of column names followed by 2 to 1024 data rows in which every cell is a finite number. Relative paths are resolved against the working directory of the Schemaxis process. The file is copied into the run directory and its digest is checked again at verification; it is fixed when the node is created and cannot vary per state. | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096}` | **required** |
| `xColumn` | Header name of the column holding the x coordinate of each path point (exact, case-sensitive match). | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":128}` | `"x"` |
| `yColumn` | Header name of the column holding the y coordinate of each path point (exact, case-sensitive match). | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":128}` | `"y"` |
| `zColumn` | Header name of the column holding the z coordinate. Leave it empty for a planar curve: every point then gets z = 0 and the table needs only x and y columns. | `{"type":"string","maxLength":128}` | `""` |
| `radius` | Radius of the tube swept along the path (Blender curve bevel_depth). | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `0.05` |
| `resolution` | Number of segments in each quarter circle of the tube cross-section (Blender bevel_resolution). 0 gives the coarsest, diamond-like section; higher values make the tube rounder and add faces. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":8}` | `3` |
| `closed` | When true the path is cyclic: a final segment joins the last point back to the first, giving a ring-shaped tube without ends. Closed paths need at least three points. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
| `caps` | When true the two open ends of the tube are filled (Blender use_fill_caps), giving a closed volume suitable for STL publication or boolean; when false the ends stay open. It has no effect on a closed path. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` |
| `centre` | World position [x, y, z] of the object origin; every CSV point is offset by it. Schemaxis assigns it as the object's location, so the mesh itself stays about the local origin and later modifiers that work about that origin (mirror, bend, twist) use this point. Keep it at [0, 0, 0] when the points are already world positions. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `smoothShading` | When true, every face of the generated curveFromCSV is marked smooth so Blender interpolates normals and the tessellated surface renders without visible facets; when false the faces render flat. Geometry and vertex positions are identical either way. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |

- `file` is a constructor option.
